title: Summer/Winter Mountain Leader (SWML) (MGySgt to Sgt) FMOS, CG TECOM
raw_text:
14. MOS 0945, Summer/Winter Mountain Leader (SWML) (MGySgt to Sgt) FMOS, CG
TECOM

    a. Summary. The S/WML possesses all the requisite skills needed to
advise units operating across all sub-environments contained within mountain
and cold weather environments. The S/WML performs duties of the unit
mountain leader who is the subject matter expert in mountain warfare tactics,
techniques, and procedures, acts as an advisor to the commander, and is
capable of conducting pre-environment training for their units.

       b.   Prerequisites.   Must be screened for G6PD and sickle cell.

    c. Requirements. Must successfully complete both the Summer Mountain
Leaders Course (M24M7A1) and the Winter Mountain Leaders Course (M24M7B1) at
the Marine Corps Mountain Warfare Training Center, Bridgeport, CA.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (dj), Mountain Warfare Operations Training and Readiness Manual.




                                          3-99                        Enclosure (1)
 3115                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Military Mountaineer, Level III; Master Military Mountaineer.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

First exposure to Marine Corps training is provided by the Drill Instructor. Next contact is with the marksmanship coaches and instructors overseen by a Range Officer, Swim Instructors, Martial Arts Instructors, and then Marine Combat Instructors. In the operating forces, training continues with the addition of Small Weapons Instructors and Martial Arts Instructor-Trainers. These MOSs are sponsored by the Training and Education Command.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
